- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#8 ("Confirmatory test of S_adj (P7) on new seeds, mechanism (g) and two new graph families") by `experiment-repo`  > **P7 confirmatory result: INCONCLUSIVE** (rule from the Brief, applied as frozen; coefficients from the 2142 original cells, committed in 9cdb893 before the block ran; nothing refitted).
  > 
  > Block: 33 runs (27 in block C, 6 in block H), new seeds and graph draws, noise level 0.5, s in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}, Tier G, n = 3000, d in {5, 20, 80}, p in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} (SBM also p = 0.1, 0.9 for (g) with the full p grid); 666 cells in 10 groups: SBM by mechanism (a)-(h) (27 cells each, (g) 45) and the two new families HK (Holme-Kim) and LN (configuration model, log-normal degrees), 216 cells each, all eight mechanisms pooled. Target: log(|realised bias| + 0.01) of the cell; predictors from a random half of the draws (as in the diagnostic).
  > 
  > Counted predictor: S_adj (parametric-bootstrap noise part) + corner x curvature.
  > - Criterion 1, absolute held-out R^2 > 0: met, R^2 = 0.115 (0.157 against the training mean). Best benchmark (p(1-p)): 0.016; the other two degree benchmarks are negative (-0.045, -0.031).
  > - Criterion 2, gain over the best benchmark >= 0.05 with the group-level bootstrap CI excluding 0: gain 0.099, 95% CI [-0.059, 0.170] (B = 2000 resamples of the 10 groups). **Not met**: the point value passes, the CI includes 0.
  > - Criterion 3, gain positive in >= 2/3 of the groups (7 of 10): **5 of 10** (HK, LN, a, c, d). Not met. (With 9 groups, without (h), it is 5 of 9 against 6 needed; same outcome.)
  > - Verdict by the Brief's rule: R^2 > 0 but the interval of the gain includes 0, so inconclusive; not "supported".
  > 
  > Per group (gain over best benchmark; R^2 of S_adj, of the best benchmark): HK +0.112 (0.082, -0.030); LN +0.158 (0.152, -0.006); a +0.278 (0.498, 0.221); b -0.060 (0.141, 0.201); c +0.070 (-0.216, -0.286); d +0.515 (0.154, -0.361); e -0.189 (-0.505, -0.316); f -0.351 (-0.048, 0.303); g -0.203 (0.104, 0.308); h -0.037 (-0.067, -0.030). Full table: `p7_groups.csv`.
  > 
  > Pattern worth saying: the score does best where the benchmark does worst (d, c, the two new families, where the degree benchmark has R^2 ~ 0 or below) and worst on (e), (f), (g), where p(1-p) already explains much (f: 0.30, g: 0.31) and (e) is badly predicted by everything (R^2 -0.5). On (e) and (f) the frozen model is worse than the benchmark. So the score carries information about bias outside its original sample in about half of the groups, not in general.
  > 
  > Other predictors in the same table (not counted in the verdict): S_adj with the null-column noise part (the exploratory definition) R^2 0.163, gain 0.147, CI [-0.024, 0.218], 6 of 10 groups positive; S_bar (pre-registered) 0.104, gain 0.088, CI [-0.077, 0.154], 5 of 10; corner x curvature alone 0.071, gain 0.055, CI [-0.144, 0.134], 6 of 10. None meets criteria 2 and 3. For reference, on the original cells under leave-one-mechanism-out the same models give R^2 -0.094 (S_adj, parametric), -0.076, -0.194 against -0.202 for the best benchmark: the confirmation is not weaker than the original out-of-mechanism result (the original held-out R^2 of S_adj was already at or below 0), and the claim "S_adj predicts the bias out of sample" cannot be made; at most "mildly informative, inconclusive". It must not be written as a confirmed predictor. The P5 verdict is unchanged (not replaced).
  > 
  > Files (next export, `results/p7/`): `p7_confirmatory.csv`, `p7_groups.csv`, `p7_cells.csv`, `p7_original_cells.csv`, `p7_frozen_coefficients.csv` with `.meta.json` (seed 20261126, B = 2000).
